wa_castle_peak_pasayten_the_drawbridge.why: v1 (Frosty/Crow Creek from Manning Park) is the first-ascent line and, by its own notes, crosses the border unlawfully, so it cannot be the recommended way. The paragraph describes it. Many parties actually reach Castle Peak via the PCT/Castle Pass, which is not a listed variant, so v0 is the lawful default rather than a verified standard.

wa_crater_mountain_standard_route.why: Paragraph is the Canyon Creek / Jackita Ridge #738 / Crater Lake trail approach (v0), the day-trip standard; v1 Devils Dome loop exists only to avoid the ford. proseClosest=1 is a word-overlap artefact.

wa_liberty_cap_ptarmigan_ridge_finish.why: Mowich Lake/Spray Park is the usual summer approach to Ptarmigan Ridge (v0 puts you on the route's own ridge from the bottom); White River/St Elmo (v1) is the early-season option before Mowich road opens. Paragraph describes both. Seasons already differ.

wa_mount_constance_north_chute.why: Paragraph is the Lake Constance trail into Avalanche Canyon (v0), the standard Constance approach; v1 Crystal Pass is the long alternative.

wa_mount_shuksan_north_face.why: v0 is labelled standard and the paragraph describes the White Salmon lodge road approach; v1 Chair 8 is a ski-party alternative with a distinct season.

wa_sinister_peak_north_face.why: Paragraph describes the standard Downey/Bachelor walk-in to the ridge camp and over the col (v0) and mentions the FA line from the west only as history; v1 is for traverse parties.

wa_accidental_discharge_east_face.why: Trip reports for Gunsight Peak (WildSnow, trailcatjim, onehikeaweek, WTA) overwhelmingly use the Stehekin ferry + Agnes Creek approach, and v1's own notes say it puts you on the glacier side this east-face route starts from. Paragraph asserts Downey Creek (v0) is standard, which the record does not support.

wa_cascade_peak_east_ridge.why: Paragraph describes the C-J Couloir start (v0), whose notes call it the most-used line on the peak; v1 Cascade Pass/Cache Glacier is the later-season walking alternative. Seasons already differ.

wa_chikamin_peak_southeast_slopes.why: Mountaineers route page, WTA and multiple trip reports climb Chikamin as a day scramble from the Mineral Creek trailhead via Park Lakes (~15 mi RT vs ~24 from Snoqualmie Pass); PCT from Snoqualmie is the multi-day option. Paragraph describes both.

wa_colchuck_balanced_rock_west_face.why: v0 notes say the outlet line is what parties who have been there recommend; paragraph describes both options.

wa_east_ridge_2.why: Only v0 is an approach (Kindy Creek roadbed and ribbon trail); v1 is a camping note on the same ground. Paragraph matches v0.

wa_glacier_peak_sitkum_glacier.why: White Chuck trail is the historic, route-defining approach to the Sitkum and the road was reopened (WTA signpost; a Feb 2025 NWHikers report reached the road end); North Fork Sauk is the longer fallback. Dec 2025 storm damage limits Glacier Peak Wilderness access now, so recheck.

wa_helmet_butte_standard_route.why: Paragraph and v0 both call the Pass No Pass break-off the standard line; v1 is the option for parties camped at Buck Creek Pass. The FR 6200 closure affects both equally.

wa_jack_mountain_nohokomeen_headwall.why: Paragraph is the East Bank Trail to May Creek (v0) with the water taxi and winter gate as asides; those are v1/v2 variants of the same line.

wa_let_it_burn.why: The outlet climbers' path (v0) is the shorter, recommended way into the west cirque below Colchuck Balanced Rock; the paragraph actually describes the Aasgard-trail / brush / gully line (v1) despite mentioning the outlet.

wa_little_big_chief_mountain_northeast_f.why: Paragraph and v0 describe the Middle Fork Snoqualmie trail to Dutch Miller Gap as standard; Necklace Valley and Pete Lake are longer alternatives.

wa_mount_ballard_south.why: Paragraph and v0 describe the Mill Creek/Azurite Pass side, which suits the South Slopes route and pairs with Azurite. But v1's own notes claim Slate Creek/east ridge is what most Ballard parties use, and trip reports (trailcatjim) do use it; that is arguably a different route (east ridge), so v0 kept at low confidence.

wa_mount_constance_finger_traverse.why: Paragraph is the Lake Constance trail and South Chute (v0), the standard approach; v1 Crystal Pass is the long alternative.

wa_mount_fricaba_standard.why: Paragraph describes Upper Dungeness to Home Lake and Constance Pass (v0), named in the route title; Royal Basin is the alternative for multi-peak parties.

wa_mount_pilchuck_standard_route.why: Paragraph describes driving FR 42 to the Pilchuck trailhead (v0); the Heather Lake start is only for when the road is gated. Seasons already differ.

wa_mount_shuksan_hanging_glacier.why: Paragraph describes the White Salmon approach (v0) and names Fisher Chimneys (v1) as an alternative used by some parties.

wa_mount_spickard_silver_glacier.why: SummitPost and most trip reports call Depot Creek from Chilliwack Lake the easiest and usual Spickard approach, and the Silver Glacier route starts at the Custer-Spickard saddle reached from Ouzel Lake; the Ross Lake boat / Silver Creek approach is less used. Paragraph gives both camps.

wa_mount_stone_putvin.why: Paragraph is the Putvin Trail to Lake of the Angels (v0), the route's namesake; v1 via Lena Lake is a long traverse alternative.

wa_mount_washington_olympic_standard.why: Paragraph is the FR 2419 Big Creek road-end approach (v0); v1 from Ellinor is for traverse parties.

wa_olympus_blue_glacier_east_ramps.why: Paragraph is the Hoh River / Blue Glacier / Snow Dome approach (v0), the standard; v1 Bailey Range is for traverse parties.

wa_sahale_mountain_sahale_glacier.why: Paragraph is the Cascade Pass / Sahale Arm approach (v0); v1 is the same line done car-to-car, a logistics variant.

wa_slippery_slab_tower_ne_face.why: Paragraph gives both trailheads; v0 Tunnel Creek to Hope Lake then PCT south to Trap Pass is the commonly described approach with less climbing and easier tread. Not independently verified on the web.

wa_south_early_winter_spire_direct_east_.why: Paragraph describes the Spire Gully approach from the hairpin (v0), with early-season snow noted in passing; v1 is the same line with snow. Seasons already differ.

wa_summit_chief_mountain_south_route.why: Paragraph describes Pete Lake and the PCT switchbacks to Vista Lakes (v0); v1 Lemah Meadow shortcut is a single-source brushy variant.

wa_the_tooth_south_face.why: Paragraph describes the summer Snow Lake trail / Source Lake / Great Scott Bowl approach (v0); v1 is the winter avalanche-terrain line with a different season.

wa_warrior_peak_standard.why: Paragraph is the Upper Dungeness / Boulder Shelter approach to the SE cirque (v0), called the shortest and easiest; v1 is the Home Lake camp option on the same corridor.

wa_cathedral_peak_last_rites.why: Andrews Creek is the common approach (Country Highpoints/SummitPost: quickest overall, paved drive from Winthrop); Cathedral Driveway is an hour-plus farther to drive and ends with 1,300 ft climbing out. Prose names Andrews Creek.

wa_dark_peak_dark_glacier_route.why: Variant 0's own notes say Swamp Creek is still what most descriptions call standard; Mountaineers TRs report Hemlock Camp is gone to beetle-kill deadfall and the Dark Fin Col climb is choked with deadfall. Prose lays out both options explicitly.

wa_lizard_mountain_south_route.why: For Lizard as the objective (South Route) the Downey/Bachelor Creek line is the shorter, 'accepted' approach per the route prose and variant 1's own notes; the Cascade Pass line is the Ptarmigan Traverse through-trip on which Lizard is a side trip.

wa_mount_daniel_lynch_glacier.why: Mountaineers Lynch Glacier route uses Cathedral Rock TH -> Cathedral Pass -> Peggy's Pond; variant 1 notes itself call Deception Pass/Dip Top Gap 'the longer, eastern line'. Prose paragraph describes the Deception Pass line. (Variant 0's season text reads like the Pea Soup approach's and may be misfiled.)

wa_mount_stuart_ice_cliff_glacier.why: Summer road-open approach via Stuart Lake TH/Mountaineer Creek is the normal line; variant 1 is only the spring gated-road version of the same walk.

wa_sloan_peak_corkscrew.why: Mountaineers trip reports overwhelmingly use Bedal Creek and recommend it (avoids the North Fork Sauk fords and overgrown Cougar Creek path); the prose calls Cougar Creek 'standard' and Bedal 'often-preferred', and describes Cougar Creek in detail.

wa_bear_mountain_chilliwack_north_buttre.why: Hannegan Pass/Chilliwack River is the standard US approach; the Canadian-side line needs a legal border crossing and is badly overgrown.

wa_castle_peak_pasayten_scramble.why: Ross Lake boat + Lightning/Freezeout Creek is the standard US approach; variant 1 notes call the Harts Pass crest-trail line the one that trades the boat for much more walking.

wa_chiwawa_mountain_southwest.why: Route is the Southwest/Standard via Trinity and Chiwawa Basin; variant 1 notes call Phelps Creek 'less-travelled'.

wa_colchuck_peak_colchuck_glacier.why: Same approach in both variants (seasonal split of glacier condition); early-season snow is the classic window for the Colchuck Glacier, so index 0 is reasonable.

wa_eldorado_peak_east_ridge.why: Eldorado Creek climbers' path in summer is the standard; variant 1 is the same line under late-spring snow.

wa_gray_wolf_ridge_se_slopes.why: Lower Maynard Burn/Baldy is the SE Slopes approach; Royal Basin variant is only for making a traverse.

wa_hozomeen_mountain_northeast_buttress.why: Skyline II trail from Silver-Skagit Road is the practical approach; the ranger-station border-swath start depends on reaching Hozomeen itself, and NPS has the Hozomeen boundary crossing closed to vehicles and foot traffic.

wa_jack_mountain_south_face.why: Canyon Creek/Crater Lake/Jerry Glacier is the standard approach; variant 1 is just an alternate camp at the end of the same approach.

wa_liberty_bell_beckey_route.why: Summer Blue Lake Trail approach is the standard; variant 1 is the same line with early-season snow.

wa_little_big_chief_mountain_west_route.why: Waptus River Trail from Salmon La Sac is the standard; variant 1 is a shortcut off the same trail for the upper part.

wa_mount_bigelow_scramble.why: Standard Scramble goes via Eagle Lakes Trail/Upper Eagle Lake; Horsehead Pass is described as the easier alternative.

wa_mount_constance_north_chimney.why: Walking the closed Dosewallips roadbed is the base case; biking it is a common way to do the same approach, and everything above the path start is identical.

wa_mount_hardy_snow_scramble.why: The Mountaineers' standard Hardy route is the South Face from the Swamp Creek pullout (4.5 mi/4,100 ft), and variant 1's own notes say most day parties go that way; the prose describes the long PCT/Methow Pass line. Medium because the route name (SW Slopes snow/scramble) could also fit a multi-day trip from Rainy Pass.

wa_mount_rainier_disappointment_cleaver.why: Paradise -> Camp Muir is the standard DC approach; Ingraham Flats is the overflow/alternate high camp.

wa_mount_shuksan_northwest_arete.why: Both options start from White Salmon lodge; variant 0 is the more direct and is described first; prose outlines both options.

wa_mount_spickard_southwest.why: Depot Creek (from the Canadian side up to the border) is the usual Silver Lake approach; Ross Lake/Silver Creek is the much longer all-US alternative.

wa_mount_stuart_cascadian_couloir.why: Summer Esmeralda/Longs Pass scramble is the standard; spring snow climb is the same line in a different season.

wa_north_face_3.why: Blue Lake Trail + Concord-Lexington gully in summer; variant 1 is the same line with early-season snow.

wa_prusik_peak_west_ridge.why: Most parties reach the Core via Colchuck/Aasgard in summer (dry); variant 1 is the early-season snow version of the same line.

wa_sharkfin_tower_southeast_ridge.why: Walk-in is identical; the variants split only on snow vs dry gully. Index 0 fine but either window is common.

wa_snowfield_peak_neve_glacier.why: Pyramid Lake/Colonial moraine camp is the standard; variant 1 is only a higher camp.

wa_south_face_10.why: Andrews Creek is the common/quickest approach (Country Highpoints, SummitPost); Cathedral Driveway is a longer drive and a climb-out finish.

wa_swiss_peak_standard_route.why: Big Beaver/Access Creek/Luna Col is the documented standard; variant 1 notes call the Bacon Creek line the alternate and off-trail, known only in outline.

wa_three_fingers_south_peak_lookout.why: USFS: FR 41 is washed out and permanently closed to vehicles past Canyon Creek bridge, ~8-9 mi below the Tupso Pass trailhead; WTA Sept 2025 TR reports a dozen bikes at the bridge. So every party now walks/bikes the road; the prose assumes a drivable road.

wa_whistler_mountain_scramble.why: Prose itself calls Option A (Rainy Pass PCT lot) the most commonly used; that is variant 0.

wa_chair_peak_northeast_buttress.why: The NE Buttress of Chair Peak is climbed overwhelmingly as a winter/spring ice-and-mixed route, so most parties take the on-snow approach. The paragraph gives the summer trail mileage but then describes the snow gully and early-season avalanche hazard of the winter line.

wa_golden_age.why: Variant 1 calls itself the longer leftward traverse and mainly the descent line, which makes the centre-route start the usual way up. The paragraph names both starting routes equally.

wa_mount_berge_southwest_route.why: For the Southwest Route, the Little Giant / Napeequa approach is the one that reaches the southwest basin directly. The paragraph lists all three approaches. The Chiwawa ford makes it late-season only, and FR-6200 has storm-damage closures.

wa_mount_maude_r1.why: Variant 1's own notes say the Entiat side is much longer and used mainly by parties already at Ice Lakes. Phelps Creek to Leroy Basin is the standard way to the north face. The paragraph describes both.

wa_north_face_left_buttress.why: On the facts, most published ascents of Castle Peak come in from Manning Park over Frosty (the paragraph calls it 'the more common approach'). But variant 1's own notes flag it as an unlawful cross-country border crossing. The caller should decide whether an app may present that approach as primary; if not, use 0 (Ross Lake/Freezeout). The paragraph describes both.

wa_south_gully_south_spur.why: Guye Peak's South Gully is known as a winter snow climb approached from Summit West through Commonwealth, and variant 1 says the summer version is 'not well loved'. The paragraph describes the Alpental/south-side summer access, which is variant 1.

wa_burgundy_spire_north_face.why: Both variants follow the same path. Variant 1's notes say camping at the 6,460 ft bench is 'the usual way this is done'. The paragraph walks the whole line to the col and only mentions the bench as the best high camp.

wa_cathedral_peak_pasayten_se_buttress.why: Andrews Creek #504 is the standard and shortest-drive approach to Cathedral Peak, and the paragraph describes it.

wa_clark_mountain_west_ridge.why: Recent trip reports (Mountaineers basic glacier climbs, WTA, NWHikers, Wenatchee Outdoors) mostly go by Boulder Pass and the Walrus Glacier. An older SummitPost/Beckey line says Walrus is 'not the most common route', which favours the non-glacier south basin (variant 0). The paragraph describes both lines from Boulder Basin.

wa_direct_north_buttress.why: Hannegan Pass to the Chilliwack is the standard US approach to Bear Mountain. The Canadian side needs a legal border crossing and an overgrown tread. The paragraph describes the Hannegan line.

wa_forbidden_peak_west_ridge.why: The south-face couloir is the standard line to the West Ridge notch for most of the season. The Cat Scratch gullies are the late-season fallback once it melts out. The paragraph describes Boston Basin and the couloir. The seasons already differ.

wa_gunn_peak_southeast_route.why: The Barclay Creek climbers' path is the summer standard, and Tailgunner is a snow-season variation. The paragraph describes variant 0.

wa_hozomeen_mountain_southeast_face.why: There is no US road, and the northern border road crossing is closed, so the Ross Lake water taxi to Hozomeen is the normal way in. The paragraph describes it.

wa_jack_mountain_southeast_ridge_direct.why: Canyon Creek to Crater Lake and the Jerry Glacier is the standard approach. Variant 1 is only a choice of camp on the same approach.

wa_liberty_crack.why: Both variants use the same SR-20 hairpin approach. Variant 1 is early-season snow conditions on it. The paragraph describes variant 0.

wa_lundin_peak_west_ridge.why: Commonwealth Basin is the classic approach to Lundin, and the Cave Ridge traverse is a less-used alternative. The paragraph describes both as standard. The seasons already differ.

wa_mount_challenger_challenger_glacier.why: SummitPost's standard route page is 'Easy Ridge/Challenger Glacier', and most trip reports (Mountaineers, CascadeClimbers) go in by Easy Ridge to Perfect Pass. Whatcom Pass is about 17 miles and still has to get around Whatcom Peak. The paragraph describes both.

wa_mount_constance_terrible_traverse.why: The Lake Constance climbers' trail is the standard approach. Variant 1 calls itself 'the long way in' for parties avoiding that trail.

wa_mount_howard_south_slope.why: Merritt Lake is described as the shorter, more direct way in. Rock Mountain is used mainly by parties combining two summits. The paragraph describes both trailheads.

wa_mount_rainier_kautz_glacier.why: The Paradise/Nisqually crossing approach is the standard Kautz approach, and Van Trump is the alternative. The paragraph describes both.

wa_mount_shuksan_white_salmon_glacier.why: The White Salmon lodge road is the climbers' approach, and Chair 8 is the ski-descent line. The paragraph wrongly routes over Austin Pass and Lake Ann, which variant 0's notes explicitly reject, so it describes neither.

wa_mount_steel_standard.why: The route is named for the Duckabush approach. First Divide (variant 1) is shorter, but the North Fork Skokomish trail is closed by Bear Gulch Fire damage between Staircase Rapids and Home Sweet Home (ONP/USFS closure notices), so Duckabush is the usable standard for now.

wa_mount_stuart_north_ridge.why: The north side from the Stuart Lake trailhead via Mountaineer Creek is the standard North Ridge approach, and Esmeralda over Longs and Goat Pass is the longer alternative.

wa_north_ridge_2.why: Whatcom Peak's North Ridge is reached from Whatcom Pass. Hannegan (west) is the more common way there because it needs no water taxi, though the mileages are comparable. The paragraph describes both.

wa_raven_ridge_southeast_ridge_crater_la.why: The route is named for the Crater Lake approach, which the paragraph describes. Libby Creek is the alternative.

wa_silver_star_glacier.why: Both variants follow the same path. Silver Star via Burgundy Col is commonly done in a day, and the bench is the standard camp only for parties who split it over two days. The paragraph covers the full line and both uses of the bench.

wa_snowking_mountain_standard.why: The Kindy Creek roadbed and Kindy Ridge is the only approach. Variant 1 is only a choice of camp.

wa_south_spur.why: The paragraph calls Easy Ridge over the Impasse to Perfect Pass 'the standard approach', and variant 1 is presented as the alternative.

wa_the_brothers_south_couloir.why: Both variants follow the same Lena Lake approach. Variant 1's notes say early season is the classic time because the gullies brush in later, and most trip reports are spring/early summer on snow. The paragraph describes the summer boot path and debris field (variant 0).

wa_trapper_mountain_north_couloir.why: Over Cascade Pass/Alliteration Col suits the couloir's snow season. The Stehekin-side approach is used by the other route.

wa_whitehorse_mountain_nw_shoulder.why: Niederprum #653 to Lone Tree Pass and High Pass is the standard route, and Snow Gulch is a deep-snow-only variant used by some ski parties.

wa_concord_tower_north_face.why: Variant 1 is the same Blue Lake line under early-season snow; the prose describes the summer walk (variant 0) with a note about early snow in the gully.

wa_inner_constance_standard.why: The route's own prose says the Lake Constance/Avalanche Canyon approach (~8 mi) is 'more commonly used' than the 16-mile Dosewallips/Constance Pass line the paragraph actually describes. Note: variant 0's notes/hazards mention the South Gully and the Thumb, which are Mount Constance features - possible cross-peak contamination worth a look.

wa_mount_cameron_standard.why: Prose labels Obstruction Point/Grand Pass the 'primary approach' and calls the Dosewallips line rarely used; variant 2's own notes agree. NPS still lists Obstruction Point Road as a seasonal mid-Jul to mid-Oct road.

wa_mount_mystery_standard.why: Route is named for Royal Basin/Deception; prose describes Upper Dungeness -> Royal Basin -> Royal Pass, i.e. variant 0. Variant 1 is framed as the option for parties already at Home Lake.

wa_phantom_peak_south_route.why: Prose describes both approaches at length; variant 0 (Hannegan/Whatcom/Perfect Pass) is described as favoured by recent parties, and Northern Pickets trip reports (e.g. Brisbine's Crooked Thumb/Phantom via Whatcom Pass) use it, versus the notorious Luna Creek bushwhack.

wa_the_direct_north_ridge_w_gendarme.why: Variant 1's own notes call Ingalls/Goat Pass 'now the common way', and Mountain Project notes it pairs with the Cascadian Couloir descent (the most common descent). The north (Mountaineer Creek) approach is favored mainly early season with a Sherpa Glacier descent (spokalpine). Prose is the generic Stuart-area text describing the Goat Pass line and only mentions Mountaineer Creek in passing.

seasonEdits.0: Jun-mid Jul; best early, while the Sherpa Glacier still gives a straightforward descent back to this side

wa_cannon_mountain_south_slopes.why: Variant 1 notes call itself 'the documented alternative' - brushy, cliffy, no trail, no published timing; Snow Lakes/Prusik Pass is the described standard and matches the prose.

wa_cathedral_rock_standard.why: Cathedral Pass trail #1345 is the standard; Peggy's Pond is a camping/Mount Daniel-combo variant. Prose describes #1345 to the pass.

wa_cloudy_peak_southwest_slopes.why: Variant 0 is named '(standard)'; prose describes Phelps Creek/Spider Gap and calls the other two longer multi-day alternatives.

wa_dome_peak_dome_glacier.why: Variant 1 notes say parties heading only for Dome use the Downey Creek side; Ptarmigan Traverse is the long way. Prose describes Downey/Bachelor Creek.

wa_glacier_peak_frostbite_ridge.why: USFS lists White Chuck River Trail 643 and Kennedy Ridge Trail 639 as INACCESSIBLE (washed out 2003, no plans to repair), so variant 0 is obsolete. Recent Frostbite trip reports (Hebert 2022, Mountaineers 2023/2025, WTA) all start at North Fork Sauk and go north on the PCT over Red Pass. Prose mainly describes the dead White Chuck/Kennedy Ridge line (variant 0), with N Fork Sauk as option 2.

wa_hagan_mountain_south.why: The Mountaineers' Blum/Hagan route page and Brisbine's Blum-Hagan traverse reach Hagan from the Blum Lakes basin over the 6,831 ft pass (variant 1). The prose's Sulphide Creek -> 'Hidden Lake' tarn -> cliffbands line ends at the Bacon-Hagan saddle tarn (Hidden Lake per Brisbine), i.e. the variant 0 line, which variant 0 itself frames as used by Watson/Bacon traverse parties.

wa_ingalls_peak_south_ridge.why: Variant 1 is the Headlight Basin camping branch; own notes say day parties take the high #1390 line. Prose describes #1390 to Lake Ingalls.

wa_kyes_peak_glaciated_scramble.why: Route title says Standard; prose describes Virgin Lake south-ridge path and names the Columbia Glacier as the alternative (variant 1).

wa_little_annapurna_south_slopes.why: Both variants are the same Aasgard line split by season; snow-free late Jul-early Oct is the normal season. Prose describes the line with snow caveats; closest to variant 0.

wa_mount_anderson_eel_glacier.why: Dosewallips/West Fork to Anderson Pass is the standard Eel Glacier approach (Mountaineers route page, WTA 2024-25 reports); Enchanted Valley is the longer western alternative. Prose describes variant 0.

wa_mount_christie_west.why: Every account uses North Fork Quinault to Low Divide; the Elwha side now carries an extra 6.2 mi road walk each way since the Olympic Hot Springs Road closure. Prose describes variant 0.

wa_mount_ellinor_standard.why: Route is named for the Upper Trailhead; variant 1 is the lower TH fallback and variant 2 the off-season chute. Prose describes the upper TH summer trail.

wa_mount_olympus_blue_glacier.why: Only one approach exists (Hoh River Trail); variant 1 is the upper-mountain glacier route, not an alternative way in. Prose covers both but is mostly the Hoh walk.

wa_mount_rainier_ptarmigan_ridge.why: Route is best May-June but Mowich Lake Road typically opens only in July (NPS); Mountain Project suggests White River may be 'just as easy' when the road is gated, and the NPS climbing-ranger blog's June report used White River/Curtis Ridge. Mowich remains the shorter approach when open, so this is a judgment on in-condition timing, not a settled standard.

wa_mount_skokomish_standard.why: Variant 0 notes: 'THIS IS THE STANDARD APPROACH'; variant 1 recorded only because waypoints describe it. Prose describes Putvin/Lake of the Angels.

wa_mount_stone_lake_of_angels.why: Route is named for Lake of the Angels; Lena Lakes/St. Peter's traverse is a 2-3 day scenic alternative per its own notes. Prose describes Putvin.

wa_mount_torment_south_ridge.why: Variant 1 notes call Torment Basin 'much less-used'; Boston Basin/Taboo Glacier is the standard and is what the prose describes.

wa_north_twin_sister_scramble.why: Prose matches variant 0 (Clearwater Creek gate, logging roads to the mile-5 cairn, clearcut spur). Variant 1 is the same Middle Fork/FR-38 logging-road network described from another start and may largely duplicate variant 0; no evidence it is the more used line.

wa_raven_ridge_standard_route.why: Route is named Libby Lake Gully-Ridge; Crater Creek is framed as the gully-avoiding alternative. Prose describes Libby Creek/#415.

wa_sinister_peak_southwest_route.why: Only one approach (Downey/Bachelor Creek); variant 1 is a camp choice, not a way in.

wa_south_arete.why: Variant 1 is the same Blue Lake line under early-season snow; prose describes the summer climbers' path.

wa_southeast_mox_peak_se_rib.why: Only one approach (Depot Creek); variant 1 is a camp choice. Prose describes Depot Creek.

wa_the_scoop_2.why: Prose presents both but calls the outlet line shorter (about an hour vs 1.5-2 h); the north-end outlet climbers' path is the usual way into the Colchuck Balanced Rock west cirque.

wa_trapper_mountain_south_slopes.why: Trip reports (WTA 2019 Trapper Lake; Engineered for Adventure via Cascade River Road) reach Trapper Lake from Cascade Pass/Pelton Basin (5,392 ft pass = Cascade Pass), i.e. variant 1. Variant 0/prose's Stehekin ferry + Harlequin start is doubtful (Harlequin is far down-valley and variant 0's own notes flag conflicting drainages/distances).

wa_wild_wild_west.why: Walking up the road from the pullout is the direct way to the West Face; variant 1 is for parties coming from routes on the far side.
